model_annotation: The plot illustrates the coverage achieved by four different language model configurations as a function of the number of completions (k), which is displayed on the x-axis on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ to 2⁸ (i.e., 1 to 256). The x-axis tick labels are spaced at powers of two, and the axis is labeled "Number of completions (k)". The y-axis, labeled "Coverage", is on a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Four lines are shown: a solid blue line with circular markers for "Llama-3B", a solid green line with triangular markers for "Llama-3B + FT", a dashed light blue line with circular markers for "Llama-1B", and a dashed light green line with triangular markers for "Llama-1B + FT". All four lines show an increasing trend in coverage as k increases. At k=2⁰ (1 completion), coverage is approximately 0.42 for Llama-3B, 0.41 for Llama-3B + FT, 0.25 for Llama-1B, and 0.24 for Llama-1B + FT. At k=2⁸ (256 completions), coverage reaches approximately 0.88 for Llama-3B, 0.87 for Llama-3B + FT, 0.85 for Llama-1B, and 0.84 for Llama-1B + FT. The Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT lines are consistently above the Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT lines across all values of k, and the fine-tuned versions (FT) are slightly below their base counterparts at all points.
